title: KL Rahul's Wellington Hundred Completes SENA Sweep, a First for an Indian Opener
excerpt: Rahul's 136 at the Basin Reserve was his first Test hundred in New Zealand, making him the first Indian opener — and the fifth Indian overall — with Test centuries in South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.
body:
• KL Rahul's 136 on Day 3 in Wellington made him the first Indian opener to score a Test century in all four SENA countries — South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.
  • He is the fifth Indian batter overall to complete the set, after Mohammad Azharuddin, Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid and Virat Kohli, and the eighth Asian batter to do it, according to ANI.
  • Rahul's hundred, Devdutt Padikkal's 80 and a fifty from captain Shubman Gill took India to 402 for 3 in the latest live score reported from the Basin Reserve, a lead of 34 over New Zealand's 368.
  • For followers in the US and UK: this is a two-match series and the match is still in its first innings on Day 3 — India's immediate job is to turn the lead into a match-winning one.

KL Rahul completed a set no Indian opener has managed before. His century on Day 3 of the first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington was his first Test hundred in New Zealand, and it gave him Test centuries in all four SENA countries — South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia — according to ANI, reported by WebIndia123.

Rahul went on to make 136 from 290 balls, with nine fours and two sixes, before Nathan Smith bowled him — the ball caught the bottom of his glove and deflected onto the stumps, according to the Daily Jagran's live coverage. In the latest score reported from Wellington, India were 402 for 3, leading New Zealand by 34 runs, with Rishabh Pant having joined Gill at the crease.

The record, in context

Rahul reached his hundred off 207 deliveries, with a single off Jacob Duffy after lunch on Saturday. It is his 13th Test century — 10 of them overseas — and his 12th as an opener, drawing him level with Murali Vijay among Indian openers. Only Sunil Gavaskar, with 33, and Virender Sehwag, with 22, have more hundreds as Indian Test openers, ANI reported.

Overall, Rahul is the fifth Indian batter to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries, joining Azharuddin, Tendulkar, Dravid and Kohli. He is the eighth Asian batter to achieve the feat, and he and former Pakistan opener Saeed Anwar are the only two batters in that group to have done it while opening the batting. Since 2021, Rahul has scored seven Test hundreds as an opener, the joint-most alongside Ben Duckett, Yashasvi Jaiswal and Dimuth Karunaratne, and his four hundreds in the World Test Championship 2025-27 cycle are level with Tom Latham and Travis Head among openers, according to ANI.

How Day 3 was built

India resumed on 159 for 1, still 209 runs behind New Zealand's 368, with Rahul on 52. He and Devdutt Padikkal added 165 runs for the second wicket, following the 130-run opening stand between Rahul and Jaiswal on Day 2 — India's first century opening partnership in Tests on New Zealand soil since 1994, according to Sportskeeda. Read our Day 2 report on the opening stand for how the platform was laid.

At lunch India were 239 for 1, Rahul on 93 and Padikkal on 53. Rahul completed his hundred after the interval, and India reached 344 for 2 at tea with Rahul unbeaten on 124. Padikkal, who had looked set for a third successive Test hundred, fell for 80 off 175 balls, bowled by Kyle Jamieson. Gill then completed his half-century with a six off Duffy — the shot that also took India past New Zealand's total — before Rahul's dismissal at 386 for 3.

New Zealand's 368 was built on Henry Nicholls' unbeaten 175 and Glenn Phillips' 118, after Jasprit Bumrah and Akash Deep had claimed four and three wickets respectively, as our Day 1 report detailed. One more mark fell along the way on Day 3: this was the 12th time all four of India's top-order batters crossed fifty in a Test innings, and only the second time outside Asia, after Basseterre in 2006, according to the Daily Jagran's live coverage.

What it means, and what is next

The record confirms what Rahul's career numbers have long suggested: he is India's most travelled century-maker of this generation, with 10 of his 13 Test hundreds scored overseas. For this match, the practical question is narrower — how large a first-innings lead India can build on Day 4 in a two-match series, with Pant and Gill at the crease and New Zealand needing wickets to stay in the game. Play continues in Wellington on Sunday.
